blocks.text: Design a home-sharing marketplace like Airbnb, where hosts list properties and guests search by location and dates and book a stay. This project's earlier calendar system solved conflict-free scheduling for one person's own calendar, rarely contended since only that one person books into it. This problem is the same underlying interval-overlap idea under a genuinely different, harder condition: many different strangers actively compete to book the exact same popular listing for the exact same desirable dates, and getting that race right, so exactly one of them wins, not zero and never two, is the actual hard problem here.

blocks.alt: A guest's search is narrowed by location and by actual date availability, and booking a listing is an atomic reservation against that listing's own calendar, safe under real, multi-guest contention

blocks.text: The technique that makes this safe is the same optimistic-concurrency, compare-and-swap pattern this project's digital wallet design used to prevent overdraft, applied here to a listing's calendar: a booking attempt reads the current availability and a version number, and commits only if that version is still unchanged, retrying safely whenever a competing guest won the race first.

blocks.text: A guest should be able to search for listings by location and a date range and see only results genuinely available for every one of those dates. A guest should be able to book an available listing, with payment captured as part of a successful booking. Two guests attempting to book the exact same listing for overlapping dates should never both succeed. A host should be notified promptly whenever one of their listings is booked.

blocks.alt: Never double-book the same dates, relevant and genuinely available search results, correctness under real multi-guest contention, fast search across a huge inventory, and trust between strangers

blocks.text: Never double-booking means two guests racing for the exact same listing and dates must never both walk away with a confirmed booking. Relevant, available search results mean a shown result has to actually be free for the requested dates, not merely nearby and appealing. Correctness under real multi-guest contention is the sharpest departure from a personal calendar, many different strangers genuinely compete for the same popular listing, unlike one person's own, largely uncontended schedule. Fast search means staying responsive across a worldwide inventory of millions of listings. And trust between strangers means guests and hosts are transacting real money and real property with people they have never met.

blocks.text: This design assumes payment processing reuses the payment system this project already covers, and focuses instead on what is genuinely new here, booking concurrency under real multi-guest contention. Every listing is assumed to support instant booking once availability is confirmed, host-approval workflows are treated as a variant on the same underlying booking mechanism rather than a separate design. Search result staleness of a few seconds to a couple of minutes is assumed acceptable, with the booking step itself, not the search step, being where strong consistency actually has to hold.

blocks.text: When two different guests both attempt to book the same listing for overlapping dates at nearly the same instant, each reads the listing's current calendar and version. Whichever commits its reservation first wins, since its compare-and-swap succeeds while the version is still unchanged; the other's attempt is rejected once it re-reads and finds the version has already moved, honestly reporting the dates are now taken rather than silently overwriting the first guest's booking.

class BookingResult:
    # The outcome of a booking attempt, including how many compare-and-swap
    # attempts it took, to make the retry-under-contention behavior visible.
    def __init__(self, status, attempts_used):
        self.status = status
        self.attempts_used = attempts_used


class Listing:
    # One listing's durable state: its reservations, sorted by start day, and
    # a version number used for optimistic concurrency control.
    def __init__(self):
        self.reservations_by_start = {}  # startDay -> (startDay, endDay)
        self.version = 0


class BookingService:
    # Manages listings with optimistic concurrency control: a booking attempt
    # reads the current version, checks for a date overlap, and commits only
    # if the version is still unchanged, retrying against fresh state otherwise.
    def __init__(self):
        self.listings = {}
        self.pending_race_listing_id = None  # one-shot hook, armed by debug_inject_concurrent_booking_once
        self.pending_race_start = None
        self.pending_race_end = None

    def create_listing(self, listing_id):
        self.listings[listing_id] = Listing()

    def debug_inject_concurrent_booking_once(self, listing_id, start_day, end_day):
        self.pending_race_listing_id = listing_id
        self.pending_race_start = start_day
        self.pending_race_end = end_day

    def try_reserve(self, listing_id, start_day, end_day):
        attempts = 0
        while True:
            attempts += 1
            listing = self.listings[listing_id]
            seen_version = listing.version

            if self._has_conflict(listing, start_day, end_day):
                return BookingResult("DENIED_DATES_UNAVAILABLE", attempts)

            # Deterministically simulate a concurrent booking landing between this
            # read and this attempt's own commit, exactly once, if armed for this listing.
            if listing_id == self.pending_race_listing_id:
                listing.reservations_by_start[self.pending_race_start] = (self.pending_race_start, self.pending_race_end)
                listing.version += 1
                self.pending_race_listing_id = None  # fire only once

            if self._compare_and_swap_reserve(listing_id, seen_version, start_day, end_day):
                return BookingResult("CONFIRMED", attempts)
            # Version mismatch: someone else committed first. Loop and retry with fresh state.

    def _has_conflict(self, listing, start_day, end_day):
        starts = sorted(listing.reservations_by_start.keys())
        before = max((s for s in starts if s <= start_day), default=None)
        if before is not None and listing.reservations_by_start[before][1] > start_day:
            return True  # preceding reservation ends after this starts
        after = min((s for s in starts if s >= start_day), default=None)
        if after is not None and after < end_day:
            return True  # following reservation starts before this ends
        return False

    def _compare_and_swap_reserve(self, listing_id, expected_version, start_day, end_day):
        listing = self.listings[listing_id]
        if listing.version != expected_version:
            return False  # the version changed since this attempt's read; reject, caller will retry
        listing.reservations_by_start[start_day] = (start_day, end_day)
        listing.version += 1
        return True

    def reservations_for(self, listing_id):
        starts = sorted(self.listings[listing_id].reservations_by_start.keys())
        return [f"{self.listings[listing_id].reservations_by_start[s][0]}-{self.listings[listing_id].reservations_by_start[s][1]}" for s in starts]


def main():
    booking_service = BookingService()
    booking_service.create_listing("listing-1")
    booking_service.create_listing("listing-2")

    # A guest books listing-1 for days 10 to 15.
    print("Book listing-1 [10,15):", booking_service.try_reserve("listing-1", 10, 15).status)

    # A conflicting booking attempt on the same listing: [12,18) overlaps [10,15).
    print("Book listing-1 [12,18), should conflict:", booking_service.try_reserve("listing-1", 12, 18).status)

    # A booking that fits exactly in the gap right after the first: [15,20).
    print("Book listing-1 [15,20), should succeed:", booking_service.try_reserve("listing-1", 15, 20).status)

    # A completely unrelated listing books its own, independent dates with no interference at all.
    print("Book listing-2 [10,15), independent of listing-1:", booking_service.try_reserve("listing-2", 10, 15).status)

    # Simulate a genuinely concurrent competing booking landing between this attempt's read and its own commit.
    booking_service.debug_inject_concurrent_booking_once("listing-1", 25, 30)
    race_result = booking_service.try_reserve("listing-1", 20, 24)
    print(f"Book listing-1 [20,24) with a simulated concurrent race: {race_result.status}, attempts={race_result.attempts_used}")

    print("listing-1's final reservations:", booking_service.reservations_for("listing-1"))
    print("listing-2's final reservations:", booking_service.reservations_for("listing-2"))

items: Architecture: geospatial-plus-availability search, and atomic, optimistically-concurrent booking against each listing's own independent calendar and version.
Capacity: millions of listings worldwide, searches vastly outnumbering bookings, and real contention concentrated on a small fraction of especially popular listings.
The core techniques: interval-overlap availability checking wrapped in compare-and-swap concurrency control, both worked through with a real, verified implementation in Java, Python, and C++.
Database: a listing-partitioned, versioned calendar store as the strongly consistent source of truth, alongside a region-partitioned, staleness-tolerant geospatial search index.
End-to-end workflows: a normal booking flow and a genuine multi-guest contention flow, both traced as sequence diagrams.
Consistency: a strongly consistent, atomic booking guarantee per listing, paired with an eventually consistent, approximate search result set.
Trade-offs: optimistic concurrency versus pessimistic per-listing locking versus no concurrency control at all, compared directly on uncontended cost and behavior under real contention.
